name: Amr ibn al-Ahtam
bio: Amr ibn Sinan belonged to the Minqar branch of Tamim in Najd and lived through the rise of Islam. His father’s damaged front tooth earned him the nickname al-Ahtam, by which the son is also known. Amr visited the Prophet Muhammad and was remembered as a public speaker as well as a poet. Al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi included his account of sheltering a night traveller in the Mufaddaliyat. Al-Zirikli dates his death to 57 AH (677 CE).
